verdict.tagline: A punishing journey where surviving the physics engine is half the battle.
for_you_if: you play with friends who can laugh at sudden physics bugs
you want an adventure that gets rewarding after a steep learning curve
not_for_you_if: you expect a smooth ride without unexpected vehicle launches
you want a clear tutorial to guide your early hours
you play primarily solo where the difficulty spikes harshly

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the physics system as inconsistent, with objects and vehicles clipping, shaking violently, or launching unexpectedly.

citations.review_text:
[h1]A physics game where the physics are the main obstacle[/h1]

Thirty minutes was enough to identify the problem. Not because I had seen everything, but because the central mechanic had already failed in every way that mattered.

[b]RV There Yet[/b] is built around moving a heavy vehicle through difficult terrain, yet neither the RV nor the objects around it behave consistently enough for that loop to work.

Take the most basic task: placing a plank. PEAK and Abiotic Factor give you a placement preview and let you put it where you intend. Here, you throw the plank at the ground and hope gravity, collision and divine intervention agree on the angle.

Trees clip straight through the RV. A winch that could barely move it one second suddenly caught on a tree and pitched the entire vehicle into the air at roughly a 60-degree angle. This is not challenging terrain simulation. It is a physics lottery.

The character physics are no better. I opened the hatch, fell out and then kept tumbling down the road indefinitely, as if the ragdoll state had no exit condition. A friend merely stood up inside the moving RV and was ejected through the vehicle.

The wildlife behaves like a collection of debug hazards. Bears attack the RV for no discernible reason, while snakes act like heat-seeking missiles, aggroing from several metres away after you throw something at them.

The item and survival systems feel equally arbitrary. The early item pool is full of junk with no obvious purpose, while many of the useful large objects cannot be secured inside the vehicle and simply bounce or clip out. Eating one raw meat patty did more damage than a bear, a snake and a high-speed fall combined, and the medical answer was an EpiPen.

Apparently food poisoning is the final boss.

This is not "funny jank". Funny jank still rests on rules consistent enough for the player to understand what went wrong. Here, you are not learning the RV or mastering the terrain. You are waiting to see what the collis…
extremely buggy, could not get past the first checkpoint after 4 restarts. Constant clipping of objects that screw up the vehicle.

Would be fun if it didet had so muych bugs.. i got problems with the RV... BEC ITS WAS ALOT ALOT OF BUGS!!... AND THE RV WAS SHAKEING LIKE HELL AND U THROWS AWAY FROM IT TO THE OTHER SIDE OF THE WORLD and when u really can be in the whole world Shakes!!....

Such a fun idea and I want to continue playing it with my friend, but maybe because I paid for it. It is buggy. While I don't mind dealing with bugs in a physics game - it can make for some fun moments. Within our first 5 minutes of the game, my friend jumped into the van and it shot into the trees. Nothing abnormal - he just tried to use the stairs and it bugged out and the game thought he was not a player and shot the RV into the trees - it looked funny - but we had to restart. Then he dropped the map in the RV and the Mix Tape - you can't pick them back up, they become one with the floor. 1 checkpoint later - winching the RV up a cliff (hence funny moments) the map landed on the back wall and I managed to pause winching, and collect it again. This stuff should not happen after so many patches have been released. It should still be in Beta or Early Access - not released. 

We will likely play a bit more until something like our initial experience reoccurs and then we will drop it until it is patched. 

Don't buy it until it has more updates! Oh, I have played through to completion frustrating games like Raft, this needs more patches.

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the checkpoint system as punishing, noting that dying forces players to repeat repair and looting tasks from earlier points.

citations.review_text:
Honestly, the game idea is extremely fun and I absolutely loved the first hour or so. However, there are some glaring issues:

1. While the jankiness is kind of expected and part of the charm, we had some really weird stuff happening like getting stuck in trees that we barely touched, winch ropes getting stuck in random geometry... It's not an issue until it resets you a few times to the last checkpoint because youre fully stuck.
2. And that's the bigger problem: sure, not being able to save the game manually and savescum is part of the appeal. However, it's also quite annoying when the game resets you all the time to BEFORE you had repaired the RV and put a bunch of work into planning. Infuriating. My suggestion: have something like the saviour schnapps in KCD - limited saving resource that allows teams to set a couple of points themselves.
3. For some reason, the game caused nausea for a few of us. Not sure why, but the movement may need to be fleshed out more. Played countless FPS so it's not a 'me' issue.

Otherwise, really liked it. I just wouldn't recommend to buy it until some of the above is fixed / addressed.

Needs way more checkpoints to be truly fun, in my opinion. Make a stupid mistake and you loose like 2h of progress. We quickly lost all enjoyment and motivation to keep on playing when that happened... Twice, on both maps.
If they solve that one major problem, I would change my review to recommended, because it's otherwise a very fun game to play with buddies!

claims.claim: Reviewers mention that the checkpoint system resets players to before vehicle repairs were completed, requiring those tasks to be redone after dying.

citations.review_text:
This game is an absolute blast with friends or to meet new people!
It is obviously extremely funny and quite cozy.
I like the whole concept of the game, the progress you make feels satisfying and each checkpoint is a massive relief.
I would just change 1 thing, when you respawn at a checkpoint, if your car was already damaged it will spawn that way again and you have to fix it before continuing and it's a Cycle.
I feel like the checkpoints should allow you to manually save when you are near them so that way you can fix up the RV, save, and then continue in the game, so that way if you have to respawn the RV is ready to go.
One of the best party games out there.

Honestly, "friendslop" fits this quite well. If you can have fun hanging out in the street with your friends, you'll probably have fun with this.

There are positives:
good concept
more content than you would think for something that was created in a "6 week game jam"
some fun and silly mechanics like smoking to run faster
a feeling of joy and pride when you finally get past whatever bull**** the game has been throwing at you for 20 mins.
an environment to "hang out" with some friends/a partner in that does create some funny moments

but there are soooo many negatives:
its a physics based game with janky physics
the map is basically useless
best way to get past several hard spots is to glitch around them
the animals are poorly coded and designed 
checkpoints saving when you first get to them is a PITA (having to repair and loot for the 10th time after dying to some stupid thing gets old fast)
weather mechanics on the second map sound cool, but in reality you end up just waiting around and wasting time (irony intended)
+many more

Game can be fun at times, but its basically a demo that sold over 4.5 million copies based off of the hype and cheap price. Sure its cheap at £7-ish but 4.5 x 7 = 31.5 MILLION! Thats a lot of money to make from a "game jam", and by the looks of it, they are not investing that back into the game.... its a real shame as it has the bones of a good game, but needs more time and work.... which they now have the capability to give, but wont.

claims.claim: Reviewers describe vehicle handling as clunky and difficult to control.

citations.review_text:
I cannot recommend RV There Yet
The game is way too unpolished right now.  
[b]Calling it "janky" is an understatement.[/b]

[h1]The Issues[/h1]
[list]
[*][b]Awful Vehicle Handling:[/b] Controlling the car feels terrible. It drives more like a heavy, clunky tank than an RV.
[*][b]Broken Collision Physics:[/b] Light contact with a tree makes your car straight-up explode. Other times you just get permanently wedged inside a tree with no way to move or get unstuck.
[*][b]Frustrating Checkpoints:[/b] The checkpoint system feels really bad. The game frequently gives you a checkpoint right before you finish repairing your car. Every time you die, you have to sit there and repeat the entire repair process all over again.
[*][b]Inconsistent Spawning:[/b] Sometimes I would spawn directly on top of a snake and die instantly. Other times, spawning in the exact same spot would put the snake somewhere else.
[/list]

[h1]Summary[/h1]
The core idea might be there, but the current state is a frustrating mess.
This game would definitely need more time in the oven to be a playable and enjoyable game.

I have tried this game several times with different friends and every single time it felt like an escort mission with an unruly metal elephant full of bugs and glitches. 

The camera controller is incredibly bugged and has consistently caused issues not only for me, but also my friends which can only be solved by fully reloading the game. The controls itself are also very rough and have caused nausea. Thanks to the few and far inbetween save points, the missions become very punishing. The game only saves when you reach a checkpoint with your by then torn up rv. So every time you die and reload the game you have to do the repairs all over again, which becomes nothing but a pointless chore.
The rv often randomly glues itself to trees when you only lightly brush against them and the coding for bears, snakes and other threats feels very bare bones. There’s a lot more that I could complain about, but you catch the drift by now.

Overall this game feels like a mere game jam project or a prototype at best. Seeing that it has gotten no quality of life improvements despite great sales makes me think it is nothing but a cash grab. Better look at other popular games to play with your friends, you will regret buying this one.

claims.claim: Reviewers describe issues with items clipping through the terrain and physics geometry.

citations.review_text: Unfortunately the game with glitchy for my friend and I who played together. Items constantly clipped through the terrain, especially vital items for repairing the RV or getting through obstacles. It made it impossible to complete a level in the game, or progress very far in the level. I was also disappointed in the game play, and found myself feeling a lack luster excitement about the game, when otherwise it has a fun premise. Ultimately returned for a refund.

Interesting concept and good execution but the game is glitchy. This is a mixed review game if I ever played one.

Pros:

-No hand holding. The game leaves it up to you to figure out what you have to do and how to make things work. There is no tutorial to follow but there is a manual for things that are not so obvious.

-The map is big and has potential. There are beautiful locations at checkpoints for you to appreciate and light a cigarette to.

-Multiplayer works really well. There are no bugs or glitches with the lobby system and its very seemless.

Cons:

-Sometimes its frustrating to navigate because of the janky physics that are part of the charm of the game. They could be refined but as is the game is also unforgiving with the saves. The tricky parts usually happen right before a checkpoint and after some progress has been made. If the checkpoint fails, you lose all progress up until then and restart from last which could be very far. 

-The gear system is failed execution. You hardly ever use higher gears because they are useless. If you lose momentum or hold in the clutch too long, the RV wont pickup from the next gear. This is realistic but makes the upper gears useless as a mechanic to have because you'll hardly ever find straight roads to gear high on. Not to mention the janky control of the gears themselves. Raise the sensitivity to make the gears easier to tolerate.

-The extra tires make no sense. You can just tighten the existing ones right up and not need to replace them. Whatever mechanic this was didn't serve its purpose clear enough.

-The gas pumps serve no purpose. It would have been nice to have a functional gas system where it runs out and you have to refill at every checkpoint. 

-The RV takes wayy too much damage from just hitting a tree. A simple scrape will bring the health down to 50 or even less. It takes a bit of time and scrap to repair but scrap can be scarce for how much damage the RV takes.

-There aren't any objectives other than …

claims.claim: Reviewers report that the second map is significantly more frustrating and difficult compared to the first map.

citations.review_text: the second map is straight up garbage, the developpers F* up the game with the second map.. make it more fun instead of frustrating dumb sh* ... First level was fun! second is NOT.

The Good
This game is stupid to the max, but in the best way. It does require a somewhat competent computer to run, but can be run at about 30 fps on a fairly budget laptop with reasonable graphics settings. As for gameplay, prepare to die laughing. This game is a wacky chaotic romp through crazy terrain with friends in a RV that can spontaneously explode. You will end up shouting as the RV falls off a cliff, debating over who is the better driver, and being jump scared by snakes all while someone is downing beers like the world is ending. Even without friends it can be very fun to try and make it through the puzzles solo (hint: the internet is your friend here). Despite being designed for two or more players, soloing the whole map is definitely possible. Also, proximity voice chat makes the funny moments even better.

The Bad
To be honest, there is not much bad about this game at all. It can be a bit buggy at times, but most of the time it makes it even more funny, such as one friend stuck in the sitting pose so they just scoot around like a deranged go kart, or the RV bouncing into the stratosphere because the winch was connected wrong. It also doesn't really have a nice middle ground between the easy map and the hard map, as even after beating the first map, the second one is frustratingly hard. 

The Short Version
This game is amazing. For less than $10, you can have a ridiculous multiplayer co-op that will have you laughing for hours at a time, and even with the occasional bug or issue, I would definitely buy again.

Really fun and relaxing game with some great maps to explore. The driving and overall atmosphere made the journey enjoyable from start to finish. The only downside is that updates seem to come slowly. 

This game is absolutely peak when played with friends , you'll probably end up laughing your ass off at some of the random situations that happen along the way. I'd especially recommend the first map, which I enjoyed much more than the second one. 

Even with its flaws, finishing the game gave me a great feeling and a real sense of accomplishment.
Definitely worth playing with friends. 👍🚐😂

claims.claim: Reviewers note that singleplayer mode is considerably harder and less enjoyable than playing in multiplayer groups.

citations.review_text: The game is challenging, but that's what I like about it. It does lean more towards multiplayer; however, as agonizing as it is, it can be done solo. The first time I played it with friends, there were a lot of hilarious moments, but we ended up putting the game to the side for a few weeks. When the devs added achievements to the game, I picked it back up and started doing a solo playthrough (friends were either busy/didn't want to play at the time). There were only two parts where I had friends help me (end of the cave and end of the swamp) but that was pretty much it. My only negative critique is the swamp area (primarily near the end when you have to bring the RV up on the elevating platforms; the platforms are so narrow that it is nearly impossible for solo players to get pass this without falling into the pit. In multiplayer, it is simple--one person stays in the RV, while the other cranks the wheel. However, in solo player it is very finicky and difficult and you have to perform extra steps to get the RV up. I would have no issue if it wasn't for the pit of death that could eternally trap you if you don't have a bunch of crates to get you out. Plus, if you need to reset it'll reset you midway through the swamp. I just think devs should think about the solo gamers who play this game on that part. Despite the frustrating swamp biome, everything else is great. Plus, the ending......omg (INCREDIBLE!).
amazing game takes hours to get boing and amazing in multiplayer but singleplayer is too hard and not as fun

claims.claim: Reviewers report that minor bumps against trees or rocks can cause the RV to explode, destroying protection items while replacement parts are scarce.

citations.review_text:
The Good
This game is stupid to the max, but in the best way. It does require a somewhat competent computer to run, but can be run at about 30 fps on a fairly budget laptop with reasonable graphics settings. As for gameplay, prepare to die laughing. This game is a wacky chaotic romp through crazy terrain with friends in a RV that can spontaneously explode. You will end up shouting as the RV falls off a cliff, debating over who is the better driver, and being jump scared by snakes all while someone is downing beers like the world is ending. Even without friends it can be very fun to try and make it through the puzzles solo (hint: the internet is your friend here). Despite being designed for two or more players, soloing the whole map is definitely possible. Also, proximity voice chat makes the funny moments even better.

The Bad
To be honest, there is not much bad about this game at all. It can be a bit buggy at times, but most of the time it makes it even more funny, such as one friend stuck in the sitting pose so they just scoot around like a deranged go kart, or the RV bouncing into the stratosphere because the winch was connected wrong. It also doesn't really have a nice middle ground between the easy map and the hard map, as even after beating the first map, the second one is frustratingly hard. 

The Short Version
This game is amazing. For less than $10, you can have a ridiculous multiplayer co-op that will have you laughing for hours at a time, and even with the occasional bug or issue, I would definitely buy again.

Almost 40 hours to reach the end of 1 level and loved every minute of it. With two players, we coordinated, we laughed, we cussed (at mistakes and each other), and overall had a great time. 

The graphics are cartoony and fun, the characters are cute, and I appreciated finding the various glasses and hats scattered about. I do wish that the changes persisted and that if I picked up a new hat I had it on next login, or if equipping it allowed me to change my default appearance. 

In general the game is a lot of fun and pretty well done as far as the difficulty scale goes, ramping up from simple hills and tight spaces to near total darkness and the madness that is the end of the first map. The physics are neat and pretty well done, though sometimes simply bonking a tree or rock causes your entire RV to blow up losing all of your protection and with spare parts hardish to find that can be an issue.

My main gripe is the save system. Now, I'm not against the checkpoint style, in fact I think it's a great choice for this type of game since you need to be careful and can't save every time you make it past a difficult section. The issue is that it save as soon as you enter the save point including the damage to your RV. So if you roll in with 95% damage, fix it, and the leave just to fail again, you have to re-fix that 95% of damage. every. single. time. And that gets old.

Overall, it's a lot of chaotic fun with a friend/s and will definitely push you to the limit at times.

claims.claim: Reviewers report encountering various physics bugs and map geometry issues, such as floating trees, holes leading into the void, and rivers ending in mid-air.

citations.review_text:
This game is buggier than a Bethesda game on launch day. Every attempt we uncover some new exploit or bug ranging from infinitely respawning anytime, duping any item, throwing people through walls, using items while not holding them, the in game map showing the wrong level, driving underwater because the actual "water" wasn't extended down far enough, somehow activating "hand mode" and now you can't move and the mouse only controlls your arms (i still have no idea how this one happened)

Maps are unfinished - floating trees, sides of rivers ending in the air and some holes in the floor leading into the void. Janky physics are funny until they cost you half an hour of agonizing progress. The intended solutions to puzzles are annoying and unfun so you just try to find some way to cheese past them (and usually do)

The ending sequences of the maps are the highlights and were actually fun, but because it takes so much to get there, we will never play them again. The maps felt unnecessarily long. If they made the maps half as long but put twice the effort into them and kept the ending sequences the same, i think it would have been a lot better.

Truly the john wick of rv games.

[h1] "Are we there yet? No, we're crashed in a ditch." [/h1] | 10/10 Co-op Chaos
[b] RECOMMENDED [/b]
If you are looking for a game that will test the absolute limits of your friendships while managing a chaotic road trip, this is it. My friends and I just wrapped up completing both available maps, and it was an absolute blast from start to finish.

[b] The Good Stuff: [/b]
Peak Co-op Gameplay: The game thrives on communication (and inevitable screaming). Everyone needs to have a job, whether it's navigating, keeping the engine running, or dealing with the random hazards thrown at you.

[b] Map Design: [/b] Both maps offer a great change of pace and unique challenges. Clearing them felt incredibly rewarding after a few disastrous, hilarious failed runs.

The Perfect Balance of Stress and Fun: It hits that sweet spot where things go wrong quickly, but it never feels unfair—just beautifully chaotic.

[b] Room for Improvement: [/b]
We Need More Content: Honestly, our only major complaint is that we finished both maps and immediately wanted more. The developers have a great gameplay loop here, and we desperately need a third or fourth map added to the rotation.

[b] Minor Polish: [/b] Experienced a few hilarious physics glitches along the way, though honestly, they usually just added to the comedy.

[b] Final Verdict: [/b]
If you have a dedicated crew of 2-4 friends, RV There Yet is a must-buy. It’s a perfect mix of survival, driving, and absolute panic. Here’s hoping the devs drop some new maps soon because my squad is ready to hit the road again!
